results.1: exit 0; 9 lines numbered 1–9 with no gaps. seq 1–5 import the starting file (retry, agents.coder, agents.reviewer, tags.0, tags.1; actor unknown). results.1: exit 0; 5 lines that keep their global numbers, so there are gaps: seq 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 (6=set model, 7=set temperature, 8=remove agents.coder)
results.2: all three arms: exit 0; 5 lines numbered seq 2, 3, 6, 7, 8. Two arms: 6=set model, 7=set temperature, 8=remove agents.coder. One arm: 6=remove agents.coder, 7=set model, 8=set temperature
results.3: both arms: exit 0; 5 lines numbered seq 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 (6=set model, 7=set temperature, 8=remove agents.coder)

context.in_practice: In this run, every route produced the same numbers: 1–9, gapless, starting at 1. The starting file appears as seq 1–5, and a set that doesn't change the value uses up no number. Filtered history keeps the global numbers, so it shows gaps. The only visible difference was within route 2: in one arm, replacing `agents.coder: opus` with a map logs the removal of the old value before the two new keys. Everywhere else the removal is logged after them. The file contents were identical in every arm.
context.stakes: The `seq` number is how a user or agent refers to a specific config change and reads the order changes happened in. If the numbers have gaps, repeat, or come out in a different order, it's harder to audit who changed what and to point at one change. Nothing about the config file itself is at stake.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 keeps a full copy of the history in memory, so it grows with every change. Route 2 stores nothing extra but ties `seq` to the internal event count, so it only stays gapless while each saved event is exactly one history line. No reasoning was recorded for route 3.

plan_why: Shows the seq numbers each implementation gives history lines: across a multi-leaf import, a no-op set (no events), one set that removes one leaf and creates two, a later single-leaf set, and a path-filtered history (do seqs stay global, gapless and unique per line from 1?)
routes: Keep the history log in the aggregate's state and number seq by position in that log
seq = originator_version - 1; the created/started event is not a history line
